title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Capiz Light. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Capiz Light
options.lineage: capiz shell windows in bahay na bato
options.thesis: Remaining budget as daylight through a capiz window.
options.viewport: A standard Android finance shell with the remaining budget held in a lit capiz grid.
options.risk: Decorative if the lit cells stop encoding exact budget proportions.

raised.raise: Data rigor: every figure sits in a fixed tabular column, and the lit grid is backed by exact pesos and cents.
Capture focus: the notification quick-add opens one full-screen amount pad with nothing else competing.
Orientation: the period and week are named in the ledger caption, so the headline number has a time frame.

options.label: Passbook Ledger
options.thesis: The remaining budget is the last line of a machine-printed ledger.
options.viewport: A standard finance shell where the latest balance line sits above the ledger that produced it.
options.risk: The most familiar finance pattern here; its trust is real, but it can read like a bank app rather than a personal life hub.

options.label: Constructed Grid
options.thesis: A finance screen built on a visible construction grid, where every number snaps to a cell.
options.viewport: A standard Android shell whose budget meter and transaction rows share one exposed grid.
options.case: Holds product clarity: the grid makes hierarchy and alignment exact; loses audience identification because the Dutch specimen is not the owner's money world.
options.risk: The grid can become a poster; controls must stay standard Android.

options.label: Budget Pass
options.lineage: boarding passes and live gate boards
options.thesis: A segmented budget pass above a live board that keeps changed rows lit until noticed.
options.viewport: A standard finance shell with a budget pass at top and a ranked activity board below.
options.case: Holds product clarity: summary and change states are immediate; loses audience identification because travel documents are not the owner's money world.
options.risk: The travel metaphor can feel like a costume; the board must not outrank the budget.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.thesis: The remaining budget stated as one next decision on a saturated yellow band.
options.viewport: A standard finance shell with a yellow decision band and category rows that read like gates.
options.case: Holds product clarity: one decision per band is instantly legible; loses audience identification because an airport is not the owner's money world.
options.risk: Reads as a transit app if the money hierarchy weakens.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: A pure black-and-white data field where the budget is a barcode that depletes.
options.viewport: A full-field data wall with a monospace budget column and a burn-rate curve.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the owner does not identify with algorithmic art, and the strobing black-and-white field fights daily money reading.
options.kept: Tabular data rigor: the budget and every transaction sit in exact, fixed columns.
options.risk: Unreadable as a daily tool; the inversion is hostile to state colours.

options.label: One-Tap Feed
options.thesis: One transaction owns the screen; a right rail carries the actions.
options.viewport: A full-screen transaction card with a right action rail and the next one a snap away.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it hides the month's budget picture and turns a ledger into a feed.
options.kept: Capture focus: one full-screen amount pad, nothing else competing.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: The month as a lexicon, entries ranked by apparatus and guide words at the head.
options.viewport: A black-text ledger column with a shoulder index and one chromolithographed budget plate.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the reading model is wrong for scanning money daily, and the cream-and-serif world is the category's calm default.
options.kept: Orientation: guide words name the period and position at the top of the page.
options.risk: Beautiful to read, slow to use.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean Material 3 finance dashboard: remaining budget, category progress, recent transactions, bottom navigation, FAB.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a finance app user expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
